parsed.explanation: The combined regime imposes a tier-1 universal exposure: this division bars multi-occupancy public facilities by birth sex, applies to every visitor, and is backed by a private cause of action, a trespass offence with a documented arrest, and no division-level remedy (no nondiscrimination statute, no hate-crime law). The parent regime compounds it: passport/entry scrutiny of sex markers with fraud-ineligibility leverage, documented custody abuses (denied hormones, forced labour, sexual abuse), official 'gender ideology' threat framing, and a national court allowing marker restrictions. Mitigations are partial and not traveller-facing: national hate-crime statute, three city ordinances, employment ruling, ongoing litigation. Friendly cities and dead-letter same-sex law do not offset unremedied universal exclusion plus hostile state framing.

entry_documents.exposure: National entry screens sex markers; officers may refuse and pursue lifetime fraud findings on suspected 'misrepresentation' of sex; X-marker passports blocked for renewals; trans travellers reported with confiscated or blocked passports; several foreign governments issued advisories after detentions.
entry_documents.protection: Litigation ongoing; existing X passports remain valid until expiry; visa fraud finding requires all four elements and waivers exist.
entry_documents.interaction: Document doubt at entry can escalate to investigation, detention and birth-sex custody under parent rules.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Parent-level custody harms documented: national prisoners subjected to conversion-style policies, hormone removal; immigration detainees report forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse; one documented trans visitor-relevant arrest led to 24 hours held in a men's ward.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute and employment ruling exist but do not reach custody placement; oversight not shown to remedy.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any facility trespass or document-doubt contact can route into these custodial systems.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division-wide birth-sex rule for all multi-occupancy public restrooms, changing areas and sleeping quarters, with criminal trespass exposure and a private cause of action; applies to every visitor needing these facilities.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Statutory exemptions (chaperoning, emergencies, maintenance); three city ordinances; no remedy documented changing the rule.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Division rule sits atop parent single-sex facility orders in national facilities; accommodations only where allowed locally.

care_services.exposure: Minor's gender-affirming care banned in the division; parent proposals bar public-insurance reimbursement for under-18 care; traveller with a trans minor cannot obtain care here; hospital-ward placement practice undocumented.
care_services.interaction: Care-seeking minor could become an investigation subject under parent orders targeting facilitators.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Parent state frames trans identity as 'gender ideology' threat; counterterrorism strategy targets 'radically pro-transgender' groups; schools and teachers face criminal investigation; police arrested a trans woman under a bathroom law.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several executive orders enjoined; courts remain contested; counterterrorism text excludes mere disagreement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing licenses discrimination and lowers traveller recourse.

minors_guardians.exposure: Guardian travelling with a trans minor faces division care ban, school birth-sex restroom requirement, sports ban, and parent-level prosecutorial framing of facilitation of transition.
minors_guardians.protection: Statutory 'reasonable accommodation' to a private facility for school students; court challenges pending.
minors_guardians.interaction: Minor's care or schooling contact can trigger parent-level investigation.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Division has no hate-crime statute; gender-identity violence relies on the national 2009 statute; no state incident or prosecution data; public opinion majority supports birth-sex document rules.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute; city ordinances in three cities; national employment recourse since 2020.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police in non-covered areas lack local recourse; national investigation of bias crime uneven.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No division nondiscrimination protection; facility-law enforcement frequency and litigation unresolved; division placement among worst states not independently itemised.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid passport FAQ; litigation against marker policy; city-level ordinances provide limited local recourse.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Open questions (ward placement, enforcement rates) remain; absence of data is not safety.

anchor_checks.comparison: Same core: universal birth-sex facility rule with no remedy and polite street life. This jurisdiction adds documented custody abuse, entry fraud leverage, state threat framing, and minor care/sports bans, pushing below 0.35-A's baseline but not to 0.25-level organised targeting.

0.45-A has a facility rule with no arrests and decent policing. Here the division adds a criminal trigger, a documented arrest with men's-ward detention, no state hate-crime law, and a far more hostile parent regime — so this sits below 0.45-A.

0.55-B has hostile operators but working remedies, prosecutions and no universal rule. Here remedies are absent at division level and a universal facility ban applies, so this rates materially lower than 0.55-B.

0.25-C features police extortion atop a criminalised parent. Here there is no presentation offence and no documented extortion campaign; hostility is institutional and facility-based rather than street-policing, placing this above 0.25-C.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is the union of parent and division. The division's birth-sex facility mandate is a universal, unavoidable exposure for any trans visitor, with criminal and civil levers, no working remedy, no state hate-crime statute and no nondiscrimination protection — matched by anchor 0.35-A. The parent regime does not cushion it: entry-document scrutiny with fraud-ineligibility leverage, custody practices documented as abusive, and official threat framing ('radical gender ideology') aggravate what follows discovery, and a travelling trans minor faces care bans and prosecutorial framing of facilitation. Offsetting positives — national hate-crime statute, 2020 employment ruling, three city ordinances, pending litigation — are partial and largely resident- or complaint-facing, not shown to change outcomes for visitors. Combined, this sits at the upper edge of high risk, just below the elevated band's midpoint: no organised street targeting, but an unremedied universal exclusion under a hostile state.
